Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical cavitary lesion containing a mobile intracavitary mass with an air crescent sign, which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is consistent with pre-existing apical lung disease or bullae often seen in connective tissue disorders like Marfan syndrome.
